He dresses in muted, high-quality fabrics that speak of money without announcing it. His Edgewater Prism office has real plants, soft acoustic paneling, and a specifically calibrated ambient sound environment. Everything about the room â€” and about him â€” has been designed to make people feel safe enough to be honest.

Baris Anang specializes in neural calibration for patients experiencing cognitive disruption from augmentation integration â€” a growing population in GLMZ's upper tiers, where people buy more chrome than their brains can smoothly accommodate. He is also emotionally opaque in a way that he has never had to confront because his opacity looks, from the outside, like serene professional boundaries. He is interested in his patients. He is less certain he is capable of being interested in peers. His E.L.F. devotion is performative â€” he maintains a small shrine in his office because patients find it reassuring â€” though he caught himself genuinely speaking to it once after a session that went badly, and has not examined that moment.
